questions.question:
Which of the following idiom given in the alternatives has the meaning?

Indicate an opinion by being present or absent.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3 i.e. Vote with one's feet**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"Vote with one's feet"** means to express an opinion or preference by choosing to leave or stay in a situation. (अपनी उपस्थिति या अनुपस्थिति द्वारा राय व्यक्त करना)
 
 
• **Example:** When the company introduced unfair policies, many employees voted with their feet and resigned.
 
 
• In the context of the question, the idiom is used to describe the act of indicating one's opinion by being present or absent.
 
• Hence, the correct idiom is **"Vote with one's feet" (अपनी उपस्थिति या अनुपस्थिति से राय व्यक्त करना).**
 
 
• **Example:** People dissatisfied with the service at the restaurant voted with their feet and never returned.
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3 i.e. Vote with one's feet**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Vote with one's pocketbook** (अपने पैसे से वोट करना): This idiom refers to expressing one's preference or opinion by making purchasing decisions. 
 
 
• **Example:** Consumers vote with their pocketbooks by choosing sustainable products over others.
 
 

 
• **Vote into law** (कानून में पारित करना): Refers to the act of approving or passing legislation through a voting process.
 
 
• **Example:** The parliament voted the new education bill into law last week.
 
 

 
• **Vote with one's wallet** (अपने पैसे से राय व्यक्त करना): Similar to "Vote with one's pocketbook," it means expressing opinions through financial decisions or purchases.
 
 
• **Example:** Many people vote with their wallets by supporting local businesses.

questions.question:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct meaning of the idiom.

'tout de suite'
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4** i.e. **Immediately**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"tout de suite"** is borrowed from French and translates directly to **"immediately" or "right away"** in English. (तुरंत)
 
• This idiom is used to emphasize urgency or quick action.
 
• **Example:** When I asked her to join me, she said she'd be there tout de suite.
 
• Hence, the correct meaning of the idiom "tout de suite" is **Immediately** (तुरंत).

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4 i.e. Immediately**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 1: Slowly** (धीरे) - Refers to doing something at a slow pace or gradually. 
 
 
• **Example:** He walked slowly to enjoy the beauty of the garden.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: Later** (बाद में) - Refers to doing something after some time or at a subsequent period. 
 
 
• **Example:** We can discuss the matter later when you are free.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: After the case is over** (केस खत्म होने के बाद) - Refers specifically to an action or event following the conclusion of a legal case or matter. 
 
 
• **Example:** The judge will announce the decision after the case is over.

questions.question:
In the given question, a sentence is divided into four parts and given in the alternatives (A), (B), (C), and (D). There is an error in one part. Choose the alternative containing that part of the sentence that has the error. Choosing the alternative with the error will be the answer.

The poet longed over the bygone days and mused over the time spent with friends and relatives.

options.text: bygone days and mused over the

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the choice of preposition used with the verb "**longed**."
 
• In English, the verb "**long**" (meaning to have a strong wish or desire for something) is idiomatic when followed by the preposition "**for**."
 
• The phrase "**longed for**" correctly expresses the poet's yearning for the past, whereas "longed over" is grammatically incorrect.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **Option 1** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The poet **longed for** the bygone days and mused over the time spent with friends and relatives."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: "bygone days and mused over the"** – This part is correct. The verb "**muse**" can be followed by "**over**" or "on" to mean thinking deeply or dreaming about something.
 
• **Option 3: "time spent with"** – This part is correct; "spent" acts as a past participle modifying "time."
 
• **Option 4: "friends and relatives."** – This part is grammatically sound and completes the prepositional phrase.
 
• **Bygone:** This is an adjective meaning "belonging to an earlier time" or "past," and it is used correctly here.
 
• **Collocation Tip:** Remember that we **long for** something, but we **grieve over** or **ponder over** something.

questions.question:
In the given question, a sentence is divided into four parts and given in the alternatives (A), (B), (C), and (D). There is an error in one part. Choose the alternative containing that part of the sentence that has the error. Choosing the alternative with the error will be the answer.

It was rude about the professor's daughter to have rejected the red rose which was being given by the young student.

options.text: rejected the red rose which was
being given by the young student.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the use of the preposition "**about**" after the adjective "**rude**."
 
• In the grammatical construction "*It is + adjective + [preposition] + person + to-infinitive*," we use "**of**" to indicate that the adjective describes the character or behavior of the person mentioned.
 
• The correct phrase should be "**rude of the**," as the rudeness is an attribute being assigned to the professor's daughter based on her action.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **Option 1** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"It was **rude of the** professor's daughter to have rejected the red rose which was being given by the young student."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: "professor's daughter to have"** – This part is correct; the possessive form ("professor's") and the start of the perfect infinitive are grammatically sound.
 
• **Option 3: "rejected the red rose which was"** – This part is correct. "Which" is used as a relative pronoun to refer to the rose.
 
• **Option 4: "being given by the young student."** – This uses the passive continuous form ("was being given"), which is appropriate to describe an action that was in progress at that time.
 
• **Common Error:** Many learners mistakenly use "about" or "for," but adjectives like *polite, kind, brave, mean, clever,* and *stupid* always take "**of**" when describing someone's conduct in this specific sentence pattern.

questions.question:

After reviewing the proposal, __the team decided to proceed forward with the project__, confident that it would meet the company's goals.

options.text: the team decided to proceed forth with the project
the team decided to proceed with the project
the team decided to proceed onward with the project

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The phrase "**proceed forward**" is redundant because "proceed" already implies moving forward.

questions.question:
A part of the following sentence is underlined. Choose the option that can replace the underlined part to improve the sentence. If you feel Options A, B, or C do not improve the sentence, then choose Option D: “No improvement required.”

Since the people who gave me a ride decided to leave the concert early, __so I had to take a bus home.__

options.text: so I had taken a bus home
I had to take a bus home
so I had to get a bus home

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**2**'.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__
 
• The given sentence describes a past scenario where the speaker had to take an alternative mode of transport because the people they were relying on left early.
 
• The phrase "I had to take" is grammatically correct and conveys the necessity of taking the bus in the past.
 
• Option 1 ("so I had taken") is incorrect because the use of "had taken" implies an action completed before another past event, which doesn't align with the context.
 
• Option 3 ("so I had to get") is grammatically correct but less precise compared to "take" in the context of transportation.
 
• Option 4 ("No improvement required") is incorrect as the sentence contains redundancy ("so" and "since" are both used, which is unnecessary).

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.
 
**Complete Sentence:** *"Since the people who gave me a ride decided to leave the concert early, I had to take a bus home."*

• **Option 1:** "so I had taken a bus home" is incorrect because the past perfect tense ("had taken") is unnecessary in this context.
 
• **Option 3:** "so I had to get a bus home" is less precise as "get" is less commonly used in formal contexts for transportation.
 
• **Option 4:** "No improvement required" is incorrect due to redundancy in the original sentence ("so" and "since").

questions.question: Why is climate change considered more than an environmental issue?

questions.question: Which communities suffer most from climate change impacts?

options.text: Those that contributed least to greenhouse gas emissions
Industrialized countries with high carbon footprints

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Option 2: Those that contributed least to greenhouse gas emissions.***

 
 
• The passage explicitly highlights this injustice in the first paragraph: **"Communities that have contributed least to greenhouse gas emissions often suffer the most..."**
 
• These communities are often in developing regions or vulnerable geographic areas that lack the infrastructure to defend against the **"displacement, food insecurity, and the erosion of livelihoods"** mentioned in the text.
 
• This specific dynamic is what brings **"questions of climate justice"** to the forefront of the global conversation.
 
 
 
• ***Option 1: Wealthy nations with advanced technology.***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. While no nation is immune, the passage suggests that technology and wealth often provide a buffer that vulnerable communities do not have.
 
 
 
• ***Option 3: Industrialized countries with high carbon footprints.***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. These are the countries that have **contributed most** to the problem, whereas the passage states it is those who contributed **least** who suffer the most.
 
 
 
• ***Option 4: Urban populations in developed economies.***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. Developed economies generally have more resources to mitigate the "uneven burden" discussed in the passage.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Greenhouse Gas Emissions**: These are primarily produced by industrialized nations through the burning of fossil fuels. The "carbon footprint" refers to the total amount of these gases generated by our actions.
 
• **Erosion of Livelihoods**: This refers to the loss of ways people make a living, such as farming or fishing, which are directly disrupted by changing weather patterns and rising sea levels.
 
• **Climate Justice**: This is a term used to frame climate change as an ethical and political issue, rather than one that is purely environmental or physical in nature. It relates the effects of climate change to concepts of **justice**, particularly social justice and environmental justice.

questions.question: Name one of the major obstacles to advancing efforts to counter climate change.

options.text: A global unity and support for sustainability for all nations
Widespread adoption of renewable energy resources or 'green' technology
Political hesitation and powerful economic interests that favor short-term gains
Open government and climate policies that include everyone across all sectors

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Option 3: Political hesitation and powerful economic interests that favor short-term gains.***

 
 
• The passage explicitly identifies this obstacle in the second paragraph: **"Political hesitation and strong economic interests still slow down real action..."**
 
• It further elaborates that these interests often prioritize **"short-term profits"** over **"long-term sustainability,"** creating a barrier to meaningful environmental policy.
 
• This conflict leads to **"public frustration"** and a lack of trust in the institutions that are supposed to manage the climate crisis.
 
 
 
• ***Option 1: A global unity and support for sustainability...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The passage mentions that progress is **"slow"** and that a **"shared moral commitment"** is still needed, implying that global unity is a goal or a missing requirement, not an obstacle.
 
 
 
• ***Option 2: Widespread adoption of renewable energy...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The adoption of "green" technology is a **solution** to climate change. The passage notes that technology alone isn't enough, but it isn't listed as an obstacle.
 
 
 
• ***Option 4: Open government and climate policies...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The text advocates for **"policies that include everyone and are fair"** as a necessary step forward. These are positive developments, the opposite of an obstacle.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Short-termism**: In economics and politics, this refers to an emphasis on immediate profit or quick results at the expense of long-term health, security, or sustainability.
 
• **Lobbying and Economic Interests**: Industries that rely on fossil fuels often have significant "economic interests" in delaying climate action, which the passage identifies as a primary cause for slow progress.
 
• **Institutional Trust**: When political leaders hesitate to act on scientific evidence due to economic pressure, it erodes the public's confidence in the government's ability to solve large-scale problems.

questions.question: According to the passage, what main change in development priorities is being suggested?

options.text: Making economic growth the top priority, even if it harms the environment
Increasing industrial growth to keep up with growing global consumer demand
Letting technology replace ethical and social considerations altogether
Focusing on long-term sustainability instead of short-term profits and economic interests

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 4**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Option 4: Focusing on long-term sustainability instead of short-term profits and economic interests.***

 
 
• The passage concludes by advocating for a fundamental shift in how the world operates. It specifically calls for **"a major change in development priorities so that long-term sustainability comes before short-term profits."**
 
• This suggestion addresses the root cause of "slow progress" mentioned earlier in the text—namely, that **"strong economic interests"** currently prioritize immediate financial gain over the health of the planet and social justice.
 
 
 
• ***Option 1: Making economic growth the top priority...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The passage identifies this exact mindset (prioritizing growth over the environment) as an **obstacle** to solving the climate crisis.
 
 
 
• ***Option 2: Increasing industrial growth...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The text argues for **sustainability** and ethical policies, which often require regulating or transforming industrial growth rather than simply increasing it.
 
 
 
• ***Option 3: Letting technology replace ethical and social considerations...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The passage explicitly states, **"we cannot rely only on technology to solve climate change,"** and stresses the need for a **"shared moral commitment."**
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sustainability**: This involves meeting our current needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet theirs. It balances **environmental protection**, **social equity**, and **economic viability**.
 
• **Short-termism**: A focus on immediate results (like quarterly profits or election cycles) that often leads to neglecting long-term risks, such as environmental degradation or resource depletion.
 
• **Shared Moral Commitment**: The passage suggests that because climate change is an "ethical challenge," purely technical or economic solutions will fail without a global agreement on what is "fair" (Climate Justice).

questions.question: Why can't technology alone solve climate change?

options.text: Technology has no role in reducing emissions
It requires moral commitment, fair policies, and priority shifts

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Option 3: It requires moral commitment, fair policies, and priority shifts.***

 
 
• The passage explicitly argues that while technology is a tool, it is insufficient on its own. It states: **"we cannot rely only on technology to solve climate change."**
 
• The text lists three essential non-technical requirements: a **"shared moral commitment,"** **"policies that include everyone and are fair,"** and a **"major change in development priorities"** (prioritizing sustainability over short-term profits).
 
• This is because climate change is defined not just as an environmental problem, but as a **"social and ethical challenge"** involving **"climate justice."**
 
 
 
• ***Option 1: Technology has no role in reducing emissions.***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The passage implies technology is part of the solution but emphasizes that it cannot be the *only* solution.
 
 
 
• ***Option 2: Technology always increases carbon emissions.***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The passage does not claim technology is the cause of emissions; it identifies **"human activity"** and **"economic interests"** as the primary drivers of the crisis.
 
 
 
• ***Option 4: Innovation and sustainability cannot coexist.***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The passage suggests that for innovation to be effective, it must be guided by **"long-term sustainability"** rather than short-term profit.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Techno-optimism**: This is the belief that technology alone can solve all social and environmental problems. The passage critiques this view, suggesting that without **ethical frameworks**, technology may not address the "uneven burden" placed on vulnerable communities.
 
• **Social Equity**: The "policies that include everyone" mentioned in the text refer to ensuring that the transition to a green economy does not leave behind those who are already suffering from displacement or food insecurity.
 
• **Global Responsibility**: Because the effects are "far from evenly shared," the passage argues that nations have a moral obligation to act collectively, rather than waiting for a technological "silver bullet."
